messages.content: What parameters do the viscous friction force depend on, and in which case should it be taken into account for the physical pendulum model? In your response the last word of each sentence must become the first word of the next sentence.

message.content:
The viscous friction force depends on the angular velocity of the pendulum.
Velocity is directly proportional to the magnitude of this resistive force.
Force also relies on a specific damping coefficient inherent to the system.
System characteristics determine the value of that coefficient.
Coefficient values vary based on the fluid medium surrounding the object.
Object motion through air or liquid generates the drag effect.
Effect becomes significant when the oscillation amplitude is large.
Large amplitudes often indicate high initial energy in the setup.
Setup conditions require precise measurement for accurate modeling.
Modeling accuracy improves by including this dissipative term explicitly.
Explicitly adding it accounts for energy loss over time.
Time evolution shows the gradual decay of the swing.
Swing duration shortens as the system loses mechanical energy.
Energy dissipation transforms kinetic motion into heat.
Heat generation confirms the non-conservative nature of the interaction.
Interaction with the environment cannot be ignored in real-world scenarios.
Scenarios involving long observation periods demand this correction.
Correction ensures the theoretical prediction matches experimental data.
